name: Kingsmere City

location.about: An old cathedral city of about 250,000 in Hampshire, built round the royal mere where Saxon kings kept their summer court. A market city, then a railway and printing city; now offices, students and commuters - and a football club that has been up and down more than any other big club in the country.

colours.story: Sky blue for the mere on a summer's day, with navy - the colour of the cathedral school, whose old boys founded the club in 1874.

home.shirt: sky blue with navy collar and navy cuffs

rivals.why: the port twenty miles down the river - city against coast since 1882
the 1966 title race, lost on the last day at home to Castleford

history.title: The first champions
history.text: Founded in 1874 by old boys of the cathedral school. Association Cup winners in 1880 and 1898 - and the first champions of the League in 1889. Champions again in 1910.

history.title: City's cups
history.text: The Association Cup in 1929, 1950 and 1964, the League Cup in its first year, 1961, and the title in 1936 - but second in 1951, 1955 and, painfully, 1966, beaten to it on the last day by Castleford.

history.title: Champions and Europe
history.text: Champions in 1969, the Association Cup in 1970, the League Cup in 1976, and the club's only European trophy: the Continental Shield in 1988. The League Cup again in 1992.

history.title: So near
history.text: Second in 1995, 1999, 2001 and 2002 - four times the runners-up in eight seasons - with the Association Cup in 2001 to show for it. Then the money ran out: relegated in 2005.

history.title: The yo-yo years
history.text: Won the League Cup in 2009 as a Second Division club, promoted as runners-up in 2010, down again in 2014 - and back up through the play-offs in 2018.

history.title: The miracle
history.text: The League Cup in 2019 and then, two years after coming up, the title in 2020 - the greatest season in the club's history. The Association Cup came in 2026.

honours_note: League seasons are given by the year they ended (1889 = 1888-89).

legends.name: Arthur Pennington
legends.note: Captain of the first champions in 1889.

legends.name: Eddie Marsh
legends.note: The 1969 title, the 1964 and 1970 Association Cups. The Marsh Stand is named after him.

legends.name: Sofia Okonkwo-Reid
legends.note: Saved the club from administration in 2016 and appointed the manager who won the title.

legends.name: Liam Foster
legends.note: The 2020 title's star - promoted with the club in 2018.

records.attendance: 66,780 v Northwick FC, Association Cup sixth round, 1938 (old Mere Road)

badge.about: The crown for the Saxon kings who held court here; the mere's waters; the cathedral spire; 1874 for the year. Motto 'Regis ad Exemplar' - after the example of the king.
badge.design: A sky-blue shield with a thin navy border. At the top a gold crown. In the centre a white cathedral spire rising from three wavy navy lines for the mere. '1874' in navy beneath. 'KINGSMERE CITY' arched above the shield in navy capitals, and a navy ribbon beneath reading 'REGIS AD EXEMPLAR' in white.

ground.name: The Mere
ground.former: Mere Road (1890-2008), by the cathedral - now houses and a park, the old centre spot marked by a bench

stands.name: Marsh Stand
stands.features: the main stand: tunnel, dugouts and boxes; Eddie Marsh's statue in the plaza

stands.name: Lakeside
stands.features: two tiers facing the main stand, with the mere itself just behind it - the stand's glass back wall looks out over the water

stands.name: Cathedral End
stands.features: the home end - one big single tier; the cathedral spire in view over the roof

stands.name: South Stand
stands.features: away fans in one corner; built with room for a second tier

ground.roof: a continuous white roof on a steel frame
ground.surroundings: the mere right behind the Lakeside stand, with boats and a waterside path; the cathedral spire and the old city to the north; new housing and a railway line to the south
ground.atmosphere: a modern bowl, a bit quiet in the bad years - but the Cathedral End found its voice in the title season

for_the_engine.notes: a modern bowl - room to play
